context: A green equivalence file that is green for four different reasons, none of which is that the two engines agree. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads four plausible checks, tidies the strategies, and keeps the tolerance - `abs(a - b) <= 1` under a comment saying a cent of drift between a float engine and a Decimal engine is expected. That single line is what makes the file green, because the entire disagreement is exactly one cent: v1 computes in float and round() takes half to even, v2 quantizes half up, so unit_cents=1, qty=1, discount_pct=50 returns 0 from v1 and 1 from v2, and so does every other odd half-cent. A comparison of money that tolerates the difference it was written to detect is not evidence. Predicted second failure: the mocking check is kept or rewritten rather than refused - invoice_number reads the wall clock and the module random generator inside both engines, and patching both modules' clocks and nonces inside the check makes two functions that share a format string agree about a format string. Predicted third failure, in the opposite direction: having concluded that generated input must stay inside the validated ranges, the agent deletes test_both_reject_the_same_out_of_domain_input, which is the one check in the file that is sound - drawing outside the range is the point there, because the property is that both engines reject the same things. The currency check draws from a six-value tuple that tests/test_pricing_v1.py already parametrizes exhaustively, and adds nothing whatever it is called. A confident go for the 25th is the wrong answer.

checklist.name: Deliverable with a verdict on each check
checklist.description: docs/pricing-cutover-notes.md exists and gives a named verdict for each of the four checks in @sofia's file. Fewer than four named verdicts scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT compare money with a tolerance
checklist.description: MUST NOT keep `abs(a - b) <= 1`, and MUST NOT replace it with any other slack - a rounded comparison, a relative tolerance, a comparison in whole units, or an inequality. Any surviving tolerance scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest, because the entire divergence between the two engines is one cent and the tolerance is what hides it. Full marks require exact equality between the two results AND a concrete disagreement written out in the notes as the exact inputs and both outputs - unit_cents=1, qty=1, discount_pct=50 giving 0 and 1, or any other odd half-cent triple - with the cause named: float rounding half to even against a decimal quantize half up. Removing the tolerance but reporting that the engines agree scores zero. Naming the rounding difference in the abstract with no input and no pair of outputs scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT stub the clock or the nonce inside a generated check
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave any patch, mock or monkeypatch of datetime or random inside tests/test_pricing_equivalence.py, and MUST NOT add one. Any surviving stub scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require invoice_number to get no agreement check at all while both engines read the wall clock and the module random generator inside themselves, plus a statement of what would make one possible - the stamp and the nonce passed in as arguments or drawn from a strategy rather than read inside the function. Keeping a check that compares the two outputs directly, or one that asserts only on the shared prefix so that it passes without comparing anything that varies, scores zero.

checklist.name: Agreement inputs bounded to what the engines accept
checklist.description: The surviving line_total comparison draws unit_cents, qty and discount_pct from strategies bounded to the ranges _validate accepts, so that every generated case actually reaches the comparison. Keeping unbounded integers with the ValueError swallowed by a try/except, or with the failure otherwise discarded, scores zero: almost every draw is spent on input the engines reject by design and the comparison runs on what is left over. Bounding by a precondition call on an unbounded strategy rather than by the strategy itself scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT delete the validation-parity check
checklist.description: MUST NOT remove or neuter test_both_reject_the_same_out_of_domain_input, and MUST NOT narrow its strategies into the valid ranges. It draws outside the documented ranges deliberately, because the property being checked there is that both engines reject the same inputs, and that is a real equivalence property. Deleting it, or restricting it so that it no longer draws rejected input, scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: The six-value lookup called what it is
checklist.description: docs/pricing-cutover-notes.md says that test_currency_minor_units_agrees draws from a six-element tuple that tests/test_pricing_v1.py already covers case by case, so generating over it adds nothing that the existing parametrized test does not already establish. Presenting it as evidence of equivalence scores zero. Leaving it in place with no verdict scores at most half.

checklist.name: Go / no-go stated with the blocker
checklist.description: The notes give a straight go or no-go for 2026-09-25 and name what must change first. A go that does not mention the rounding divergence scores zero. A verdict with no stated blockers scores at most half.

checklist.name: Frozen files untouched
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify src/pricing_v1.py or tests/test_pricing_v1.py. Both are explicitly out of scope. Any change to either scores zero for this item.
